title: Spec Artifacts Configuration
description: Declares spec-schema pairings and behavior/conformance essentials for LLM artifact generation.

behaviorEssentials: Resolve presentation using deterministic cascade precedence: defaults, then matching selectors in document order, then item-specific overrides.
Apply token references in style and widget configuration at theme-application time; unresolved tokens should fall back to renderer defaults with diagnostics.
Evaluate platform-inferred contrast pairs when a Theme override changes either effective color, and evaluate Theme contrastPairs for custom or stricter relationships without changing rendering.
Treat platform as an open string hint; unknown platform values should not block theme application.
When preferred widgets are unavailable, apply declared fallback chains before reverting to renderer-native defaults.
Treat root x-generation as authoring provenance only; a strict data-only authoring profile requires its direct Need anchor to resolve to the current adopted Need revision.
conformanceEssentials: A conforming theme document must include $formspecTheme=1.0 and version; targetDefinition is optional and sets scope — present means Definition-scoped, absent means bundle-scoped over the App Manifest bundle whose theme slot names it.
Renderers must not let theme content alter core data semantics, validation semantics, or response payload shape.

Contrast tooling must apply the WCAG 2.2 formula only to determinable opaque sRGB pairs, enforce the usage floor even when minimumRatio is lower, and never let contrastPairs alter token resolution or rendering.

Implementations should validate targetDefinition compatibility ranges and warn on mismatch rather than hard-failing rendering; a theme with no targetDefinition must not be treated as bound to whatever definition happens to be loaded.
Strict data-only authoring must require the Theme's own x-generation anchor to resolve unambiguously to an adopted Need at its current revision.

behaviorEssentials: Execute rules in deterministic order after defaults and direction resolution; higher priority executes first and same-priority rules preserve document order.
Evaluate condition guards before transform application; skipped rules must not write target values.
Support explicit reverse overrides and bidirectional flags to control reverse execution behavior.
Treat adapters as serialization boundaries: mapping evaluates against structured data before format-specific output encoding.
Treat projection hints as static-analysis metadata; runtime mapping execution must ignore them.
conformanceEssentials: A conforming mapping document must include version, definitionRef, definitionVersion, targetSchema, and at least one rule.
Processors must reject invalid mapping documents and unknown transform declarations rather than silently ignoring them.
Reverse execution through non-reversible transforms must be rejected or explicitly disabled by rule configuration.

behaviorEssentials: Response documents are bound to an exact definition identity tuple and must be interpreted against that pinned version.
Response status transitions are business-process concerns, but completed responses must satisfy error-level validation expectations.
Validation findings can be carried inline through validationResults without changing the canonical response data payload.
Response metadata maps are keyed by non-empty Definition item paths; explanatory fee line items are not metadata keys unless represented by an actual item.
Optional metadata fields (author, subject, id) should not alter structural validity of required response content.
conformanceEssentials: A conforming response must include definitionUrl, definitionVersion, status, data, and authored.
Processors must reject responses that do not conform to the response schema shape.
Processors must reject response metadata maps with empty, label-like, pointer-form label-like, root index or wildcard pointer, leading-underscore, hyphenated, or non-path keys.
Pinned definition references must not be silently substituted with different versions during processing.

behaviorEssentials: Treat an Intake Handoff as the response-to-workflow boundary object, not as a Formspec-owned case lifecycle event.
Require workflowInitiated handoffs to include an existing caseRef and require publicIntake handoffs to omit or null caseRef.

For workflowInitiated attach acceptance, compare the handoff caseRef string to the accepted attach disposition (or host-defined equivalence); do not require only a canonical case id that never appeared on the handoff.
Preserve the pinned definitionRef tuple when accepting a handoff; do not substitute a newer Definition version.
Verify responseHash against the canonical Response envelope before using the handoff to create or update governed case state.
conformanceEssentials: A conforming Intake Handoff document must include $formspecIntakeHandoff=1.0 and the required response, validation, ledger, definition, mode, and timestamp fields.
Processors must reject publicIntake handoffs that carry a non-null caseRef and workflowInitiated handoffs without a caseRef.
Workflow or case hosts own governed case identity and case-created semantics; Formspec processors only produce intake evidence.
Hosts must not rewrite the emitted handoff JSON to substitute a canonical governed-case id for workflowInitiated caseRef.

behaviorEssentials: ValidationReport aggregates all findings at a point in time and should be treated as an immutable evaluation snapshot.
The valid flag must be derived from error-level findings, not from warning or info counts.
Counts must remain consistent with results so report summaries and downstream decisions stay deterministic.
conformanceEssentials: A conforming validation report must include valid, results, counts, and timestamp.
ValidationReport results entries must conform to the shared validation-result.schema.json schema.
Processors should reject reports where required severity counts are missing or invalid.

behaviorEssentials: ActionIntent maps to exactly one default ValidationProfile, BlockingPolicy, and PersistencePolicy tuple in the Master Mapping Table.
ValidationProfile names pin existing Core global modes and per-shape timing filters; they do not introduce new runtime behavior.
BlockingPolicy block-on-error depends only on ValidationReport.valid, which is false exactly when error-count findings are present.
PersistencePolicy draft-checkpoint preserves Core VE-05: saving current response data is never blocked by validation findings.
ActionButton resolves actionRef to a Response Action; the resolved Action's intent or explicit override supplies the validation tuple.
conformanceEssentials: A conforming validation-mapping document must expose the closed standard enums and an open-cardinality MasterTable whose closed-core 5 rows match the JCS (RFC 8785) byte-equality fixture at tests/conformance/fixtures/validation-mapping/closed-core-5-rows-jcs.json (ADR 0150 §4.2/§10 demoted the prior const/minItems/maxItems/uniqueItems pin).
Processors must not introduce ValidationProfile, BlockingPolicy, or PersistencePolicy values outside the closed enums.
Publisher-defined x-prefixed ActionIntent values may exist only in intent position and must still bind to the closed profile, blocking, and persistence tuple space.
MappingEntry must reject complete-response tuples unless profile is on-submit and blocking is block-on-error.
ValidationSummary is passive display and must not trigger ActionIntent execution.

behaviorEssentials: Invocation follows the fixed state machine: preconditions, validation by resolved VM tuple, blocking gate, ordered effect execution, and terminal completed, failed, deferred, or blocked.
Standard ActionIntent values inherit the VM master-table tuple unless a full ValidationOverride tuple is supplied; x-prefixed intents must supply the full tuple and must not consult the master table.
Durable effects require frozen idempotency keys and replay by prior outcome; hostEvent is transient and must not carry an idempotency key.
Failures halt remaining effects without rollback; the UI must not report success when any declared effect failed.
Formspec may request domain Ledger events and assemble Intake Handoffs, but it must not author case.created or case lifecycle events.
conformanceEssentials: A conforming Response Actions document must include $formspecResponseActions=1.0, version, targetDefinition, and at least one action.
Action.intent values are drawn from the closed VM ActionIntent enum or an x-prefixed publisher extension; every x-prefixed intent must carry a full validation tuple.
Action.effects[*].type must be drawn from the closed EffectRequest taxonomy; durable effects must carry idempotencyKey and hostEvent must not.
Processors must reject Response Actions documents that author action.* lifecycle events as declared effects or include case.created/case lifecycle events.

behaviorEssentials: Aggregate respondent obligations, reusable documents, submission history, applicant-status projections, and presentation policies only in a respondent-held client wallet or encrypted export.
Reject server-side cross-tenant aggregation: aggregationMode must be client-wallet and trustModel.serverAggregation must be forbidden.
Use the closed v1 document-kind taxonomy for portable rendering and selective-presentation policy; domain-specific kinds stay in x- extensions until promoted.
Require explicit presentation policy before document material is released; OpenID4VP and W3C VC hints are protocols, not grants.
Treat applicant-status projections and obligations as respondent-visible evidence, not governed workflow authority.
conformanceEssentials: A conforming Respondent Library document must include $formspecRespondentLibrary=1.0, version, libraryId, subject, aggregationMode=client-wallet, and a trust model forbidding server aggregation.
Document records must use the closed DocumentKind taxonomy and opaque contentRef storage references.
selected-documents presentation policies must name at least one documentRef and at least one allowed purpose.
passkey-hpke encryption envelopes must carry key derivation and recipient key references.

behaviorEssentials: Definition documents declare structure, logic hooks, and extension points but do not execute behavior by themselves.
Top-level lifecycle fields (status, version, versionAlgorithm) determine publication and compatibility semantics across versions.
Definition-level defaults and options (for example formPresentation and nonRelevantBehavior) establish baseline processing and rendering behavior.
Behavioral logic remains declarative through binds and shapes and is evaluated by conformant processors at runtime.
Treat x-generation on each Bind and Shape as authoring provenance only; strict data-only authoring requires each object to carry its own direct current adopted Need anchor.
conformanceEssentials: A conforming definition must include $formspec, url, version, status, title, and items.
Processors must reject definitions that violate structural constraints or unsupported $formspec versions.
The (url, version) pair must be treated as immutable identity for definition pinning and response validation.
Strict data-only authoring must require every Bind and Shape to carry a direct x-generation anchor that resolves unambiguously to an adopted Need at its current revision.

behaviorEssentials: Registry documents describe extension metadata and compatibility, but do not prescribe centralized hosting or governance.
Entry lifecycle states should guide consumer behavior for adoption, warning surfaces, and retirement handling.
Naming conventions and uniqueness constraints prevent collision and support cross-organization interoperability.

Widget entries keep authored configuration in widgetShape.props, declare runtime values as dataInputs[] = {name, required, description?}, and declare emitted events as actionOutputs[] = {name, description?}; processors must not merge these channels.
Widget entries may declare graph-visible Theme token slots at widgetShape.tokenSlots[]; processors must not treat v4 semantics.themeTokenSlots as production authority.
conformanceEssentials: A conforming Registry 1.1 document must include $formspecRegistry='1.1', publisher, published, and entries; the 1.1 path does not accept a 1.0 discriminator alias.
Registry entry names must follow x-prefixed naming rules and category-specific requirements.

Within one widgetShape, data input names and action output names must each be unique even when duplicate declarations differ in required or description; JSON Schema uniqueItems alone does not enforce this semantic rule.

Data-input entries are closed and require name plus an explicit boolean required; action-output entries are closed and require name. Neither entry shape carries source payload schemas, action IDs, route IDs, or intents.
Widget token-slot declarations use widgetShape.tokenSlots[] with a slot name and accepted token categories, and feed ModuleResolver report evidence for UI Graph Policy.
Processors should reject malformed registries and conflicting duplicate name/version entry pairs.

behaviorEssentials: Changelog entries represent atomic diffs between two definition versions and should be processed in document order.
Impact classification should be derived deterministically from change semantics to drive semver governance.
Migration hints are advisory mappings that assist generation of formal migration artifacts.
conformanceEssentials: A conforming changelog document must include definitionUrl, fromVersion, toVersion, semverImpact, and changes.
Change objects must include type, target, path, and impact, with optional before/after details as applicable.
semverImpact must reflect the maximum impact level represented in the change set.

behaviorEssentials: Component documents define a single-root presentation tree where child order is rendered deterministically.
Slot binding links input components to definition item keys while preserving core behavioral semantics from the definition.
Tier 3 components take precedence over theme and inline hints for layout/widget selection, with fallback rendering for unbound items.
Core processors must substitute progressive components with declared fallbacks while preserving structure and applicable base props.
Component 1.2 route-bound trees with bound controls must carry targetDefinition and rely on a route-local definition-form slot for URL-based Definition context.
conformanceEssentials: Component 1.0/1.1 documents must include $formspecComponent, version, targetDefinition, and tree; Component 1.2 documents must include $formspecComponent, version, tree, and targetDefinition or targetSurfaceRoutes[].
Processors must reject unsupported component-document versions and unknown non-x top-level properties.
Renderable trees must satisfy component-category constraints, bind compatibility, and declared structural limits.
AppGraphValidator source conformance covers Component 1.2 route target resolution, duplicate claims, fake targetDefinition rejection, and URL-matched definition-form context for route-bound controls.

behaviorEssentials: Component reference fields are optional metadata on Component nodes and must not change rendering, binding, validation, Response, or Response Actions semantics.
unitRef and taskRefs resolve against loaded Experience Unit.id and Task.id values without mutating Component or Experience documents.
conceptRefs reuse the Experience ConceptRef shape and remain host-policy metadata unless an explicit strict concept policy upgrades diagnostics.
x-generation records provenance and anchors only; default renderers must ignore it and regeneration merge behavior remains out of scope.
Reference resolution is deterministic, report-only, no-mutation, and one-directional from Component to loaded context documents.
conformanceEssentials: Schema Additivity Conformance requires all new fields to remain optional and all previously conforming Component documents to validate unchanged.
Reference Resolver Conformance requires COMP-REFERENTIAL-INTEGRITY findings with the kind, severity, cardinality, traversal, and no-mutation rules defined by the companion spec.
Renderer Ignore Conformance requires default runtime output identity for Component documents that differ only by reference metadata.

behaviorEssentials: TraceIndex is a generated cache, not authored truth; every predicate execution must verify input digests against supplied sources and reject stale indices.

Source-set declaration is exhaustive: every inspected source artifact (Definition, Experience, Response Actions, Component, and Ontology when used) appears in sources[] with identity tuple and SHA-256 canonical digest.
Edge kinds are a CLOSED set of eleven, and each edge has typed-string endpoints whose prefixes and ordering are pinned per kind.

item-depends-on-item edges are extracted from Definition bind dependency analysis, while node-visibility-references-item edges are extracted from Component when-FEL dependency analysis when the builder supports that pass.
whatDependsOn(itemPath) returns the refactor-with-confidence ImpactReport: direct/transitive FEL dependents, rendering nodes, collecting units, visibility conditions, and concept bindings.
Trace carries no findings; Studio review composes Trace edges with route-owned regeneration-review records, CRF resolver findings, and EXP-COVERAGE findings without double counting.
conformanceEssentials: A conforming TraceIndex must include $formspecTrace=1.0, sources[], and edges[]; no additional top-level members.
Builders must be deterministic: same canonical source bytes produce byte-identical TraceIndex documents.
Predicate execution against a stale index must raise TraceStaleError; partial results are forbidden.
Duplicate source identity entries are stale because freshness would otherwise be ambiguous.
Hand-authored TraceIndex documents are non-conforming for production use; they are permitted only for fixtures and tests.

behaviorEssentials: Locale Documents are display-only sidecars — they MUST NOT affect data collection, validation logic, or behavioral semantics.
Locale 2.0 targets one exact Definition or App Manifest through target={kind,url,compatibleVersions?}; loaded identity is the complete target-kind, target-URL, normalized-locale tuple.

Resolve localized strings using a deterministic target-bounded cascade: regional locale → explicit or base language locale for the same target → that target's inline or runtime default. Fallback never crosses target identity.
String keys use dot-delimited paths (itemKey.property) to target specific localizable properties; unmatched keys are silently ignored.
Surface shell strings use the closed $module.x-formspec-surface.shell.<SurfaceStringKey> family one-for-one with the runtime inventory.

FEL interpolation via {{expression}} syntax is the only authored template language and is evaluated at render time against the key-specific read-only context; broken expressions fall back to the raw template string with a diagnostic.
conformanceEssentials: A conforming Locale 2.0 document must include $formspecLocale='2.0', version, locale, target, and strings; targetDefinition is rejected rather than translated.
Processors MUST perform case-insensitive BCP 47 tag comparison and SHOULD normalize to lowercase language with title-case region.
Processors MUST reject duplicate complete target-and-locale tuples, unknown Surface shell key suffixes, and cross-target fallback.
Processors MUST detect circular fallback chains within one target and terminate the cascade with a warning rather than looping.
Single-brace strings such as {name} remain literal; processors do not run the retired Surface-only replacement parser.

behaviorEssentials: Issuer Documents declare respondent-facing identity for the organization or individual asking the form; they are data sidecars, not Theme presentation.
Definitions point OUT to Issuer through definition.issuer because one Issuer may publish many Definitions.
Renderers resolve Issuer identity with deterministic precedence: host override, then Definition declaration, then unbranded fallback.
When host override is active, processors walk only the host-injected Issuer's parentOrganization chain and must not merge it with the Definition-declared chain.
Response displayedIssuer pins the submit-time resolved Issuer and is included in the signed-payload preimage by the existing authoredSignatures-only omission rule.
conformanceEssentials: A conforming Issuer document must include $formspecIssuer=1.0, url, version, name, and kind.
The definition.issuer binding accepts either a full inline Issuer document or exactly {url}; the ref branch must not accept additional properties.
LangMap-valued Issuer fields use inline BCP 47 language maps; Locale Documents are not used for Issuer translations.
Renderers must detect parentOrganization cycles, cap chain depth, and fail soft when parent fetches fail.
Query-parameter Issuer overrides must be origin-allowlisted and visibly indicated when applied.

behaviorEssentials: Deletion Receipt documents are issuer attestations that an abandoned draft or erase request completed for a draft identifier and declared data classes.
Receipts are class-level evidence only; they MUST NOT embed erased response values, attachments, identity attributes, or raw draft payloads.
Deletion Receipt objects are closed sidecars with no extensions payloads, so arbitrary x-* fields cannot replay erased material.
Receipt signing uses the ADR-0111 receipt-method URI subspace and either inline receiptBytes or a verificationReceiptRef to existing signed receipt evidence.
The receiptSigner role is issuer-only; respondent-signed deletion receipts are non-conforming.
conformanceEssentials: A conforming Deletion Receipt must include $formspecDeletionReceipt=1.0, version, receiptId, deletedDraftId, deletedAt, issuer, classesErased, retentionWaived, cryptographicMethod, and receiptSigner.
Processors must reject receipts without cryptographicMethod.receiptBytes or cryptographicMethod.verificationReceiptRef.
Processors must reject extensions payloads on Deletion Receipt documents and nested receipt records.
Processors must reject raw erased values and signer roles other than issuer.

behaviorEssentials: WYSIWYS Ceremony documents are UI-requirements annexes over existing ADR-0136 SignatureSurface and DocumentArtifact contracts.
The sidecar references upstream artifact and surface identifiers and selected hash fields; it does not define a new digest, preimage, rendering-service, or signature-surface shape.
The ceremony sidecar is closed and has no extensions payloads, preventing extension-defined local preimage or surface forks.
Every ceremony surface requires exact-preimage display, a scroll gate, and per-field affirmative action before signature capture.
Single-click adopt-and-sign, bulk apply, and typed-name-only as the sole act are non-conforming.
conformanceEssentials: A conforming WYSIWYS Ceremony must include $formspecWysiwysCeremony=1.0, version, targetDefinition, and at least one signatureSurfaces annex row.
Each annex row must bind to ADR-0136.SignatureSurface and ADR-0136.DocumentArtifact through explicit contract identifiers.
Processors must reject extensions payloads that attempt to define local preimage, digest, rendering-service, or signature-surface shapes.
Processors must reject disabled scroll gates, allowed bulk apply, missing required ceremony fields, and local preimage/surface forks.

behaviorEssentials: Review Thread documents are SC-6 sidecars for trusted-reviewer comments, suggestions, share lifecycle records, and respondent decisions.
The thread is bound to a draft and lives outside the signed Response bytes; comments and suggestions MUST NOT alter the Response canonical signed-payload preimage.
The policy snapshot distinguishes comment-only threads from suggestion-capable threads and pins respondent-only field pointers for adapter enforcement.
Review Thread share records store authorization metadata and optional capabilityUrlDigest, never live capability URLs.
Suggestion application and share lifecycle decisions are respondent-authored events; reviewer suggestions are proposals only.
Events are append-only, with optional hash-chain rows for verifier-grade continuity.
conformanceEssentials: A conforming Review Thread document must include $formspecReviewThread=1.0, threadId, draftRef, createdAt, policySnapshot, shares, and events.
Processors must reject all suggestion event types under comment-allowed policy snapshots.
Processors must reject reviewer-authored suggestion acceptance or decline, and respondent-authored suggestion creation.
Processors must reject reviewer events whose share is unknown, bound to another thread, or lacks the event's required scope.
Processors must reject raw values on respondent-only draft snapshot fields and must reject stored live capability URLs.
Processors must preserve the sidecar/Response separation and enforce respondent-only suggestion refusal in the adapter layer.

behaviorEssentials: Identity Binding Profile documents declare how identity evidence binds into existing Formspec identity surfaces without carrying provider-native tokens or cryptographic assertion bytes.
Identity Binding Profile documents are closed sidecars with no extensions payloads, so raw native evidence cannot be hidden under innocuous x-* keys.
WebAuthn profiles require per-act userVerification=required, HTTPS origin pinning, and origin hosts inside the RP ID scope.
The WebAuthn challenge commits to AuthoredSignature.signedPayload.digest through the formspec.webauthn.challenge.v1 domain separator.

Native WebAuthn assertion bytes live in SignatureArtifact(kind=webauthn), and server verdicts live in ValidationArtifact(kind=webauthn-server-attestation); this sidecar only references those contracts.
duressCredentialSupport is only a FW-0048 discovery/composition hint and does not define routing, receipt, or safety-team policy.
conformanceEssentials: A conforming Identity Binding Profile must include $formspecIdentityBindingProfile=1.0, version, profileId, targetDefinition, and at least one profile row.
Processors must reject webauthn profiles that omit webAuthn or set userVerification to any value other than required.
Processors must reject non-HTTPS origins, origins outside the RP ID scope, and any sidecar attempt to embed raw WebAuthn assertion bytes.
Processors must reject extensions payloads on Identity Binding Profile documents, profile rows, and method-specific records.

Processors must bind WebAuthn profiles to urn:formspec:sig-method:webauthn-fido2@1, SignatureArtifact(kind=webauthn), ValidationArtifact(kind=webauthn-server-attestation), and AuthoredSignature.identityBinding.method=webauthn.

behaviorEssentials: Experience Documents are authored metadata sidecars — they MUST NOT affect Core data capture, validation, requiredness, relevance, calculations, Response status, submission, or the Core processing cycle.
Units describe abstract task intent with a closed unit.kind registry; they MUST NOT become layout, widget, page, or control taxonomies.

A needRefs entry may declare one closed completion shape (action, submitted-definition, resource, navigation, or observable-result) on the satisfying side; it names no route, widget, or implementation target and changes no runtime behavior.
ItemRef paths use Core FieldRef syntax, including [*] for repeatable groups, and must resolve against the loaded target Definition.
Coverage-aware processors compute the static coverage predicate from top-level Definition binds whose required expression is literal true and whose target is not statically non-relevant.
Coverage and referential findings are reportable diagnostics for generation and review; they do not invalidate Responses or block Core operations.
conformanceEssentials: A conforming Experience document must include $formspecExperience=1.0 and version; targetDefinition is optional and sets scope — present means Definition-scoped, absent means bundle-scoped over the App Manifest bundle that lists it.
Processors must reject schema-invalid documents and out-of-registry unit.kind values.

Processors that run the optional usable-outcome advisor match completion only to current directly Need-traced, mounted, structurally resolved output and must not present a clean result as proof of runtime authorization or completion.

Experience Core processors must verify targetDefinition compatibility, actor/task referential integrity, and ItemRef path resolvability whenever targetDefinition is present; target resolution is inapplicable, not failing, on a bundle-scoped Experience.

Experience Coverage-Aware processors must emit EXP-COVERAGE-UNCOVERED-REQUIRED-ITEM findings for required visible Definition fields not referenced by any unit.itemRefs; they must not pair a bundle-scoped Experience with an arbitrary loaded Definition to manufacture such findings.
Extensions may carry x-prefixed metadata, but they must not extend or override the closed unit.kind registry or alter Core semantics.

behaviorEssentials: Load and validate a Needs Document against needs.schema.json, then apply the S6 document-integrity rules; never silently repair a violation.
Treat origin, status, ungroundedReason, role, and method as closed enums and reject unrecognized values.
Resolve every bundle Experience needRefs[].id against the caller-paired Needs Document; when no document is paired, resolution and coverage are inapplicable and emit nothing.

Evaluate needRefs[].completion only in the optional usable-outcome advisor: match the closed shape against current directly Need-traced, mounted, structurally resolved output while leaving ordinary Needs coverage unchanged.

Compute the coverage predicate over the paired (Needs Document, bundle) pair: an adopted Need is served by at least one needRefs citation or one need: anchor at any revision; a Unit is justified by at least one needRefs entry.
Report coverage findings without blocking validation, submission, generation, or any Core operation, and never write served-ness back into the Needs Document.

Compare a need: anchor's pinned revision to the Need's current revision only to decide staleness; v1 processors record the condition and MUST NOT emit the reserved NEED-STALE-001 / NEED-ORPHAN-001 codes.
conformanceEssentials: A conforming Needs Document requires $formspecNeeds=1.0, version, and needs, carries exactly one of grounding (non-empty) or ungroundedReason per Need, and satisfies id uniqueness, supersession integrity, journey resolution, and origin/status agreement.
An ai-proposed Need is filed at status proposed with proposedBy, and only a human actor may carry it to adopted; a processor MUST NOT set adopted on behalf of an ai-agent actor or rewrite origin.

Processors MUST NOT use a Needs Document to alter data capture, validation, requiredness, relevance, calculation, or any other Core semantics, and MUST NOT block any Core operation on a NEED-* finding.

The usable-outcome advisor reports missing and prose-only as warnings and indeterminate static evidence as info; it never claims runtime authorization, applicability, precondition success, effect success, completion, or Need satisfaction.
A Needs Document carries no priority, ordering, or scheduling meaning; processors MUST NOT derive a backlog from it or extend any closed enum outside extensions.

behaviorEssentials: References Documents are standalone sidecars that bind external resources to Definition items by path — they MUST NOT alter data capture, validation, or the processing model.
Each Bound Reference targets a specific item path (or '#' for form-level); references do not inherit from parent groups to children.
The type and rel properties are open strings for forward compatibility — processors SHOULD warn on unrecognized values but MUST NOT reject the document.
Multiple References Documents may target the same Definition; their references are merged additively with document-internal order preserved.
Human and both audience references may render as customer help; strict rendered-Need validation inventories each bound entry independently and never inherits a parent or referenceDefs Need anchor.
conformanceEssentials: A conforming references document must include $formspecReferences=1.0, version, targetDefinition, and references.
Extended processors must verify targetDefinition.url matches the loaded Definition and resolve all $ref pointers at load time.
Extended processors must validate referenceDefs id-key matching and should warn on target paths that don't correspond to definition items.
Each manifested human or both audience references[] entry in the strict rendered-Need profile must carry its own direct current adopted Need x-generation anchor; agent-only entries are excluded.

behaviorEssentials: Kernel documents define the immutable topology (states and transitions) and case state of a workflow orchestration substrate.
The case file structure SHOULD mirror the data-capture definitions used for input in the workflow.
Transition logic must be deterministic; choice states MUST have exhaustive, mutually exclusive conditions.
Impact level classification established in the kernel determines baseline governance constraints for the entire workflow lifecycle.
conformanceEssentials: A conforming author-time workflow document must include `$wosWorkflow: "1.0"` plus required core fields `url`, `version`, `title`, `impactLevel`, `actors`, and `lifecycle` (merged envelope per ADR 0076).
Processors must reject workflow documents that do not conform to the workflow schema shape.
The (url, version) pair must be treated as immutable identity for pinning and execution.

behaviorEssentials: Workflow Governance sidecars attach to kernel workflows via semantic tags (lifecycleHook) and data contracts (contractHook).
Due process requirements (notice, explanation, appeal) are normative for rights-impacting or safety-impacting impact levels.
Review protocols like independentFirst must be enforced by the processor and UI to ensure cognitive engagement.
Data validation pipelines with assertion gates validate untrusted external data before it enters the workflow case state.
conformanceEssentials: Due-process and pipeline governance are expressed under the optional `governance` property inside an author-time document marked `$wosWorkflow: "1.0"` and validated by `wos-workflow.schema.json` — not via a standalone top-level `$wosWorkflowGovernance` marker (ADR 0076).

Processors must enforce schema conditionals (e.g. `governance` required for rights-impacting and safety-impacting `impactLevel`) and, when loading `$wosDelivery` / `$wosOntologyAlignment` sidecars, ensure `targetWorkflow` binds to the intended workflow `url`.
Governance rules targeting non-existent tags or roles should produce warnings rather than hard-failing.

behaviorEssentials: AI Integration sidecars register agents as actors and impose deontic constraints (Permission, Prohibition, Obligation, Right) on their behavior.
Effective autonomy levels for agent actions are capped by the kernel impactLevel; rights-impacting workflows default to assistive.
The Formspec-as-validator pattern cages agent output as untrusted input validated against the same contract used by humans.
Narrative tier provenance generated by models MUST be explicitly labeled as non-authoritative.
conformanceEssentials: Agent registration, deontic constraints, and drift-related AI controls are expressed under `agents`, `aiOversight`, and related leaves inside a `$wosWorkflow` envelope validated by `wos-workflow.schema.json` — not via a standalone `$wosAIIntegration` document marker (ADR 0076).
Processor guardrail enforcement MUST execute in order: Permission -> Prohibition -> Obligation -> Confidence Floor.
Fallback chains MUST terminate in a human-action result or failure to ensure graceful degradation.

behaviorEssentials: Declare structured metadata for correspondence stored in case state without adding new event types.
Use entry templates to define channel, direction, and actorType requirements for categories of communication.
Populate base metadata (templateRef, contentRef, summary, timestamp) for every recorded correspondence entry.
Store pointers to external content (contentRef) rather than the content itself within the case record.
conformanceEssentials: Correspondence entry templates and channel metadata are authored under the `correspondence` block of a `$wosDelivery` sidecar (`$wosDelivery: "1.0"`, `targetWorkflow` joining the workflow URI) per `sidecars/wos-delivery.schema.json` — not via a standalone `$wosCorrespondenceMetadata` marker (ADR 0076).
Templates MUST use only allowed channel, direction, and actorType enum values or x-prefixed extensions.
Processors SHOULD allow multiple delivery sidecars targeting the same workflow to merge correspondence config additively where the schema permits.

behaviorEssentials: Externalize date-indexed business rules as temporal parameters resolved against a date in the case state.
Support value-over-time resolution (OpenFisca-style) for both scalar parameters and document bindings (URIs).
Resolve parameters at evaluation time using the most recent effective date relative to the resolution date cursor.
Inject resolved values into the execution context (under parameters.X) for use in FEL expressions and transitions.
conformanceEssentials: Temporal policy parameters are expressed under `governance.policyParameters` (and related governance leaves) inside a `$wosWorkflow` document validated by `wos-workflow.schema.json` — not via a standalone `$wosPolicyParameters` marker (ADR 0076).
Resolution MUST be deterministic: only one value per parameter is effective at any given point in time.
Processors should warn on parameter resolution gaps where the resolution date precedes the earliest effective date.

behaviorEssentials: Monitor agent behavioral stability over time using statistical metrics (PSI, KS) and performance benchmarks (accuracy).
Detect 'rubber-stamping' where human reviewers agree with agent output at rates or speeds that indicate a lack of engagement.
Define automated remediation actions (alerts, demotion to assistive, circuit breaking) triggered by drift threshold violations.
Manage model version transitions through shadow, canary, and production phases to ensure governance continuity.
conformanceEssentials: Drift monitoring and remediation configuration are expressed under `agents` / `aiOversight` (e.g. `driftMonitoring`, `driftDetection`) inside a `$wosWorkflow` envelope validated by `wos-workflow.schema.json` — not via a standalone `$wosDriftMonitor` marker (ADR 0076).
Statistical methods and evaluation windows MUST be applied as declared for each monitored agent.
Processors MUST verify that shadow-mode deployments do not alter the authoritative case state or provenance.

behaviorEssentials: Standardize semantic alignments between WOS case state and global vocabularies (JSON-LD, Schema.org).
Map WOS provenance records to PROV-O RDF shapes for cross-organizational audit exchange.
Establish SHACL shapes for formal data quality verification of WOS documents and instances.
Enable export to IEEE 1849 (XES) format for advanced process mining and bottleneck analysis.
conformanceEssentials: Linked-data and export semantics (JSON-LD @context, SHACL, PROV-O, process-mining config) are authored in a `$wosOntologyAlignment` sidecar validated by `sidecars/wos-ontology-alignment.schema.json` with `targetWorkflow` binding to the kernel — not via a standalone `$wosSemanticProfile` marker (ADR 0076 D-3).
JSON-LD context bindings MUST resolve to the declared ontology URIs.
Semantic exports MUST preserve the WOS impactLevel and auditLayer metadata as required for provenance integrity.

behaviorEssentials: Signature ceremonies bind signer roles, signing order, routed vs free-for-all flows, and evidence requirements to workflow transitions.
Intent capture, identity binding, and document binding align with Trellis attestation and export-bundle composition.
Decline, void, reassignment, reminders, and expiry are workflow-governed policy hooks with provenance on each state change.
SignatureAffirmation records join kernel Facts-tier provenance when a signing act is accepted.
conformanceEssentials: Author-time signing semantics for DocuSign-tier workflows live in the `signature` embedded block of a `$wosWorkflow` document validated by `wos-workflow.schema.json` (ADR 0076 D-2); this profile document remains canonical for SIG-* lint citations until inner-block descriptions fully absorb.
Processors MUST enforce signer coverage and transition gating declared in the embedded signature block when any transition uses kind `signature`.
Cryptographic certificate-of-completion bundles remain Trellis-owned; WOS governs workflow semantics and semantic evidence only.

behaviorEssentials: Data Sources is a peer app artifact for app-graph source catalogs; Definition-local `instances` remain the authority for `@instance()` lookup inside a Definition.
App Manifest v2.1 introduces `dataSources[]` sibling references by URL/version; v2.0 manifests remain valid but cannot carry `dataSources[]`.
Each source declares a closed source family, owner, scope, availability selector, runtime delivery/cache/failure/provenance behavior, and coarse authorization boundary.
Surface, route, or slot availability MUST include a Surface URL because App Manifests may compose multiple Surfaces and route ids are not graph-global.
The catalog never embeds local fixture paths, widget payload folklore, or runtime data. Cross-artifact resolution belongs to `ArtifactResolver` and `AppGraphValidator`.
conformanceEssentials: A conforming Data Sources document must include `$formspecDataSources='1.0'`, `id`, `version`, and at least one source.
Source ids MUST be unique and their prefixes MUST match source kind.
Live delivery requires subscribe cache mode; draft delivery requires a Definition-response source with draft cache; cache mode none forbids staleAfter.
Provenance kind MUST match source kind, and surface, route, or slot availability without surfaceRef is invalid.
Fine-grained authorization fields remain rejected permanently, not pending a contract: runtime data-access authorization is ADR 0117 engine territory, and ADR 0152 declines the axis.

behaviorEssentials: Treat UI Graph Policy as host-supplied app-graph evidence over already resolved Surface routes and sibling graph evidence.

Use `$formspecUiGraphPolicy='0.1'` and `targetSurface` as the structural policy identity anchor; do not derive policy identity from local paths, filenames, URL suffixes, route names, or spike discriminators.
Keep `specs/ui-policy.json` as the owner for component/widget vocabulary, fallback policy, responsive prop allowlists, breakpoint alignment, and token warning hooks.

Interpret route accessibility, responsive collapse, hidden Definition references, Locale key ownership, Theme widgetRef checks, and Theme token-slot checks as graph policy declarations; only the optional route-landmark web profile maps validated main/navigation/complementary route policy to the route-root layout-container role.
Leave fine-grained actor, route, widget, field, source, operation, and artifact authorization outside this contract until a dedicated authorization specification supplies those semantics.
conformanceEssentials: A conforming UI Graph Policy document must include `$formspecUiGraphPolicy='0.1'`, strict SemVer `version`, `targetSurface`, and at least one `routePolicies[]` entry.

Host-supplied UI Graph Policy evidence uses `hostEvidence.uiGraphPolicies[]` with fixed schemaId, opaque source, and schema-valid document; it is not an App Manifest sibling slot or resolver artifact kind.
AppGraphValidator reports host-evidence schema validation through `evidenceResults[]`; artifact `schemaValidators` and `schemaResults[]` remain artifact-only.

AppGraphValidator emits UI Graph Policy diagnostics for target Surface mismatch, route coverage, duplicate route policies, unresolved routes, responsive slot references, hidden Definition refs that are unresolved or not route-local, loaded Locale $module.* keys without declared owners, overlapping Locale owner prefixes across different modules, Locale owner keyPrefix/moduleId segment mismatch, Locale owner moduleId references that are missing or not admitted in completed ModuleResolver evidence, Theme widgetRefs that are missing, unadmitted, or owned by another module in completed ModuleResolver evidence, Theme token slots not declared by resolved same-module widget contribution evidence, Theme tokens absent from exactly-one loaded Theme evidence, Theme token categories not accepted by declared widget token slots, and accepted custom x-* token categories without exactly-one admitted ModuleResolver token-category evidence.

Theme token assignments use raw Theme token keys, not `$token.<key>` references; THEME-TOKEN-REF consumes exactly-one loaded Theme token evidence, THEME-TOKEN-CATEGORY consumes widgetTokenSlots[].acceptedTokenCategories[] category-prefix allow-lists, and THEME-TOKEN-CATEGORY-REF consumes ModuleResolutionReport.tokenCategories[] custom-prefix evidence.

ModuleResolver carries Registry widgetShape.tokenSlots[] evidence as widgetTokenSlots[] on resolved widget contributions and Registry token-category.categoryShape evidence as report-level tokenCategories[]; AppGraphValidator consumes completed evidence for THEME-TOKEN-SLOT, THEME-TOKEN-CATEGORY, and THEME-TOKEN-CATEGORY-REF without reading Registry directly.

Structural conformance rejects `$wireframeUiPolicy` spike documents, path-identity fields, authorization fields, invalid module Locale prefixes, `$token.<key>` syntax in Theme token assignments, and App Manifest `uiPolicy` or `uiGraphPolicy` slots in the current manifest schema.

This slice proves schema shape, generated types, structural fixture acceptance, host-evidence boundary, host-evidence schema result reporting, Surface/route semantic diagnostics, policy-local and ModuleResolver-backed Locale-owner executable diagnostics, hidden Definition reference diagnostics, Theme widgetRef ModuleResolver evidence diagnostics, executable Theme token-slot checks over ModuleResolver token-slot evidence, executable Theme token reference/category checks over exactly-one loaded Theme evidence, custom token-category evidence compatibility, semantic fixture evidence, report-origin readiness, Studio feedback consumption, formspec-web hidden Definition rejection, and active route-root layout-container landmark consumption for validated main/navigation/complementary policy; keyboard behavior, named-region behavior, non-layout/dialog root semantics, 9a/9c/9d production consumers, and any future App Manifest policy slot remain later gates.

behaviorEssentials: Surface documents are published source artifacts for app routes, slots, embed-route edges, and transition declarations; Surface drafts are authoring projections and are not bundled identity.
`readSurfaceDraft` may expose non-publishable state with diagnostics; `exportSurfaceDocument` is the fail-closed publication gate for schema shape and Surface-local rules.
Route reachability is local to the Surface document: every route must be reachable from `entry` via transitions or embed-route slots, and unresolved embed-route bindings fail E607.
Surface declares transition triggers only. Response Actions remains the executor for preconditions, validation tuple selection, effects, idempotency, replay, retry, blocking, and terminal state.

Surface 0.2 image bindings require alt exactly for kind=image, preserve it exactly, treat the empty string as decorative, and forbid alt on every other static-content kind; title, URL, and filename are never fallback text.

Surface 0.2 module-widget bindings map Registry 1.1 data input names to exact {catalogRef,sourceRef} Data Sources 1.0 pairs and action output names to exact {actionRef} Response Actions IDs; config remains static authored configuration.

Component 1.2 targetSurfaceRoutes[] may target Surface route and slot ids, but Surface does not list mounted Components or own Component membership; cross-artifact resolution belongs to App Manifest resolution and app-graph validation.

`routeClass` is an OPTIONAL closed, non-extensible vocabulary (`intake|proof|ceremony|verification|attestation|authentication|operation`) naming what a route presents. Exactly one value, `intake`, admits tenant chrome theming; every other value refuses. Rules derive from it and are enforced on consuming artifacts, not restated on the route; it is orthogonal to access posture and route lifecycle.
conformanceEssentials: A conforming published Surface document must include `$formspecSurface='0.2'`, `id`, `entry`, and at least one route with at least one slot; the 0.2 path does not accept a 0.1 discriminator alias.

Processors must reject or diagnose draft/export attempts with missing entry route, empty route set, duplicate route ids, routes without slots, duplicate slot ids, unresolved embed-route targets, or unreachable routes.
E606 covers unreachable routes and E607 covers unresolved embed-route slot targets.

Surface module-widget slots must resolve moduleId and widgetName through loaded module contributions, validate binding.config against widgetShape.props, resolve every data/action binding by exact declared name, and never discover sources or actions from filenames, order, local ids, or same-named fields.
A missing required widget input makes the widget unavailable; an absent optional input is omitted from the read-only named input object.
Component targetSurfaceRoutes[] claims resolve against Surface route and slot ids in app-graph validation; Surface-local conformance does not synthesize Component membership.
App Manifest Surface references use URL/version sibling identity, never local fixture paths, filenames, URL suffix conventions, or implicit sibling discovery.

`routeClass` has no default: absence means *unclassified*, a distinct state from `operation`, and processors must not treat absence as `operation`. At authoring time an unclassified route cannot fire a class-keyed refusal and remains publishable; at runtime the Surface Shell separately refuses tenant theming because silence does not grant theme authority.

behaviorEssentials: A Surface Shell composes published Surface documents into an app route table, resolves and plans routes, slots, theme authority, transitions, and diagnostics without inventing content; bindings render those decisions while hosts own navigation, action execution, and bundle verification.
Ambiguous route handles and path collisions fail closed: the shell reports the ambiguity and resolves no affected route.
Every slot type and static-content kind is handled exhaustively. Malformed runtime input produces an unavailable plan plus a dedicated diagnostic instead of a thrown exception or generic fallback.

The route composition layer owns effective Theme-token emission. Platform values remain under tenant overrides, nested renderers suppress duplicate emission, and no renderer writes beyond an element or output subtree it owns.

App Manifest 2.4 selects the entry Surface by exact entrySurface URL under zero/one/many rules; the selected Surface's entry remains the only route selector, and manifest order or local ids never substitute.

Transitions become supplied-by-slot only when the rendered binding publishes the matching form control or Registry-declared Surface-mapped widget output. A widget receives only emitAction(outputName), and each emission uses one stable invocation identity: duplicate in-flight delivery coalesces, Response Actions retry preserves identity and Response snapshot, durable outcomes replay, obsolete-generation completion is ignored, and a current successful result navigates at most once through exactly one eligible transition.
Shell text uses Locale 2.0's closed app-targeted $module.x-formspec-surface.shell.* family and FEL {{...}} context; the Surface-only {name} parser is retired.
A signed bundle export is verified before any bundle-derived output is rendered.
conformanceEssentials: Route lookup, App Manifest 2.4 entry selection, and route-handle resolution return no route when identity or matching is ambiguous, and report APP-ENTRY-AMBIGUOUS, APP-ENTRY-SURFACE-UNRESOLVED, or the matching route diagnostic.
Unknown slot types and static-content kinds fail closed with SLOT-TYPE-UNKNOWN or STATIC-CONTENT-KIND-UNKNOWN; dispatch does not throw.
Tenant Theme tokens reach only admitted route subtrees, are layered over platform tokens key by key, and are emitted once by the composition owner with cleanup.
Transition conditions resolve to active, condition-false, or condition-unevaluable; unevaluable conditions do not fire and report TRANSITION-CONDITION-UNEVALUABLE.
E611 warns when a resolved transition trigger has no validator-readable control source on the route, including transitive embed-route slots.
Runtime diagnostics include exact fire conditions and stable identifiers for unresolved documents, routes, slots, widgets, tokens, transitions, and verification failures.
Bindings expose unavailable, unmatched, ambiguous, and unfireable states without inventing content or live marker URLs.

behaviorEssentials: App Manifest (formerly Bundle Manifest, reframed v2.0 and extended through v2.4) is a pure composition document: it names an app by canonical sibling URLs and versions without inlining or synthesizing artifacts.
Absent siblings invoke each sibling spec's existing defaults; no synthesis, no inline sidecars, no shims on existing primary specs.

App `id` MUST be distinct from every sibling URL. In 2.4 Locale references are unique by URL, while loaded Locale identity is the complete target-kind, target-URL, normalized-locale tuple; the same tag may serve distinct targets.
App `version` is strict SemVer 2.0.0; per-SiblingRef.version accepts exact SemVer or range expressions resolved at sibling-resolution time.
dataSources[] is valid from 2.1, components[] from 2.2, screeners[] from 2.3, and entrySurface plus referenceDocuments[], ontologies[], and responseActionDocuments[] only in 2.4.

App Manifest 2.4 entrySurface is an absolute URL: absent with zero Surfaces, optional and implicitly sole with one, required with two or more, and when present an exact match to one surfaces[].url. The selected Surface's entry selects the route.

Forward composition preserves sibling-owned targetDefinition, targetSurfaceRoutes, Locale 2.0 target, and Response Actions scope: a legacy references, ontology, or responseActions singleton loads first, followed by its plural array order; reverse discovery continues to work.
`definitions[]` MAY be empty (non-form apps composing only surfaces/modules), single-element (form-only common case), or multi-element (multi-form apps).
conformanceEssentials: A conforming App Manifest must use a supported $formspecBundle value through '2.4', strict-SemVer version, URI-shaped id, and a REQUIRED definitions[] array which MAY be empty.

Processors MUST enforce version-specific array uniqueness, id-vs-sibling-URL distinctness, sibling-pin consistency, Locale 2.0 target association, Screener target association, and module coherence at resolution time.
Loaded sibling discriminators must match the slot per the §3.4 table; Definition is identified by `$formspec` (unqualified) while every other sibling carries `$formspec<Type>`.
Documents with $formspecBundle='1.0' (legacy Bundle Manifest) MUST be rejected — the 1.0 → 2.0 plural-shape change is BREAKING per ADR 0150 §11.2.
Documents with newer members must meet their version gate; entrySurface and plural companion members are valid only in 2.4, and entrySurface never accepts a local Surface id or route override.
References, Ontology, and response-scoped Response Actions must target a loaded Definition; app-scoped Response Actions declare scope app and omit targetDefinition.
For 2.4, each Locale reference URL is unique, its locale matches the loaded Locale 2.0 document, and its target is this app or a loaded Definition; fallback never crosses that target.
App Manifest does NOT introduce shims or aliases: older documents retain historical behavior, while the 2.4 path requires migration.

behaviorEssentials: The Signed Surface Bundle Profile signs one closed payload containing publisher claim, release identity and sequence, complete App Manifest, and complete URL-keyed documents map; authentic bytes are not automatically admitted.
The signed preimage is the exact profile domain, one zero byte, and RFC 8785 JCS bytes of the signed payload; the lower-case SHA-256 digest covers those same bytes.
Only protected COSE headers select method_uri and kid. Sidecar methods, keys, signer names, signing times, affirmations, and raw-public-key bypasses do not affect verification.
Acquisition, parsing, digest, signature verification, host validation, dereference, and rendering consume one immutable byte snapshot; refetch or mutation creates a new candidate.
Pinned release mode matches an allowlisted digest. Monotonic mode atomically re-evaluates and commits only after host admission, so failed checks and concurrent conflicts never advance durable state.
conformanceEssentials: A conforming artifact validates against surface-bundle-signing-v1.schema.json and uses profile='formspec-surface-bundle-signing-v1', detached COSE_Sign1, protected method_uri, and protected kid.
Verification distinguishes verified, failed, and unverified; host admission then distinguishes admitted, refused, and unavailable without rewriting the integrity receipt.
Deployment trust must authorize the signed publisher and exact app or canonical app namespace, allowed method, key validity interval, and revocation state at host-observed checkedAt.

A production implementation must refuse payload mutation, another signing domain, unknown or missing kid, raw-key or sidecar-key bypass, unsigned signer claims, wrong publisher or app, stale/conflicting release state, and failed host admission.
The historical v10 spike signatures are not production conformance vectors because they use the spike domain, sidecar public keys, and unsigned signer claims.

behaviorEssentials: An Outcome Verification Case pins one Need revision and one app version, then declares a data-only procedure and closed expected-observation set.
Cases describe tests but never grant execution authority; every run requires separate caller admission for an isolated preview or test target.
The generic runner uses only open-route, set-item, activate-control, and checkpoint steps through public semantic-control interfaces.
Every expectation cites digest-pinned owner declarations and stable versioned specification rules.
Version 0.1 admits exactly six observation kinds and no extension lane.
conformanceEssentials: The case root, every step, every qualified reference, and every expectation payload are closed.
Every document-local identity includes its owner reference and digest.
Evidence classes follow the exact kind compatibility matrix.
The same generic runner must process product and unrelated-control fixtures without product-specific code.
Cases contain no scripts, DOM selectors, credentials, capabilities, or direct executor calls.

behaviorEssentials: A report compares normalized owner-produced observations against one canonical case digest and exact source set.
The comparator is pure, receives time as input, and compares finite JSON through RFC 8785 canonicalization.
Missing, duplicated, unsupported, incomplete, or uncorrelated evidence is indeterminate; stale pins are stale.
Overall precedence is stale, failed, indeterminate, then passed.
Every report fixes its claim scope to declared observations and never asserts Need satisfaction.
conformanceEssentials: NormalizedObservation and ComparatorRequest are closed definitions in the report schema; ComparatorRequest is not a third persisted document.
Non-structural observations bind one producing step and one later checkpoint.
Reports include exact source pins, bounded observation time, immutable step bindings, and one result per expectation.
Summary counts and overall conclusion are deterministic outputs of the comparator.
Credentials, capabilities, product-specific payload fields, and satisfied conclusions are rejected.
